title: Lateral plate: two layers and a cavity

objective.text: Describe how lateral plate mesoderm splits and what its two layers build.

body.general: How does the body get a wall and a gut wall? The outer strip of middle-layer tissue, the lateral plate, splits into two sheets [f1]. Between them opens a space that will become the body cavity [f4]. The outer sheet, the parietal layer, faces the amnion, the sac around the embryo [f2]. It builds limb bones, the breastbone and deep skin of the limbs and body wall [f6]. The inner sheet, the visceral layer, faces the yolk sac [f3]. With the inner germ layer it builds the gut wall [f7].
body.mbbs: Cavities in the lateral plate mesoderm merge and split it into two layers [f1]. The parietal (somatic) layer is continuous with the extraembryonic mesoderm covering the amnion [f2]. The visceral (splanchnic) layer is continuous with the mesoderm covering the yolk sac [f3]. Between them lies the intraembryonic cavity, the future body cavity, at first open to the extraembryonic cavity [f4]. The parietal layer with the overlying ectoderm forms the lateral body-wall folds [f5]. It forms limb and body-wall dermis, limb bones and connective tissue, and the sternum [f6]. The visceral layer with the endoderm forms the gut wall [f7]. Both layers give the serous membranes: peritoneum, pleura and pericardium [f8].

facts.text: Cavities in the lateral plate merge and split it into two layers.
The parietal (somatic) layer is continuous with the mesoderm covering the amnion.
The visceral (splanchnic) layer is continuous with the mesoderm covering the yolk sac.
Between the two layers lies the intraembryonic cavity, the future body cavity, at first open to the extraembryonic cavity.
The parietal layer and the ectoderm over it form the lateral body-wall folds.
The parietal layer forms limb and body-wall dermis, limb bones and connective tissue, and the sternum.
The visceral layer and the endoderm together form the gut wall.
Both layers give the serous membranes: peritoneum, pleura and pericardium.

misconceptions.wrong: The intraembryonic cavity is the gut.
misconceptions.right: The cavity is the future body cavity; the gut wall is endoderm plus visceral mesoderm.
Limb bones and connective tissue come from lateral plate mesoderm; only limb muscles come from somites.

checks.prompt: Which layer joins the endoderm to make the gut wall?
checks.why: The visceral layer faces the yolk sac and, with the endoderm, forms the gut wall.

checks.prompt: What does the cavity between the two lateral plate layers become?
checks.why: The intraembryonic cavity becomes the body cavity; the gut is built from endoderm and visceral mesoderm.

checks.prompt: Which tissue builds the limb bones and sternum?
checks.why: The parietal layer forms limb bones, connective tissue and the sternum; somites add only limb muscle.

adult: The parietal layer becomes limb bones and the sternum [f6]; both layers become the linings of the chest and belly cavities [f8].

remember.q: Which lateral plate layer helps form the gut wall?
remember.a: The visceral (splanchnic) layer, with the endoderm [f7].

remember.q: What lies between the two lateral plate layers?
remember.a: The intraembryonic cavity, the future body cavity [f4].

remember.q: Which lateral plate layer builds the limb bones and breastbone?
